status_summary: On 2025-01-24 the Acting Solicitor General asked the Supreme Court to pause briefing in four pending cases so agencies could reconsider Biden-era rules and decisions; on 2025-02-06 the Court granted the pause in the Education Department borrower-defense case and denied it in EPA v. Calumet Shreveport Refining. On 2025-02-07 a Deputy Solicitor General told the Court that the government's earlier equal-protection position in United States v. Skrmetti no longer represented the United States' view, while asking the Court to decide the case; the Court upheld the Tennessee law 6-3 on 2025-06-18. The Education case was dismissed on 2025-08-11 after the parties stipulated to dismissal. These filings show the Justice Department reconsidering prior positions at the outset of the Administration; no source found shows the White House Counsel's role in those decisions. Reuters reported on 2026-08-10 that White House Counsel David Warrington would leave and be succeeded by Will Scharf from 2026-09-01.

timeline.event: The Acting Solicitor General asks the Supreme Court to hold briefing in abeyance in four pending cases (Department of Education v. Career Colleges and Schools of Texas, Diamond Alternative Energy v. EPA, Oklahoma v. EPA and EPA v. Calumet Shreveport Refining) so the agencies can reconsider the underlying rules or decisions after the change of Administration.

The Court denies the abeyance motion in EPA v. Calumet Shreveport Refining (later argued 2025-03-25 and decided 2025-06-18) and grants the pause in Department of Education v. Career Colleges and Schools of Texas.

A Deputy Solicitor General letter to the Court in United States v. Skrmetti (No. 23-477) says the government's earlier equal-protection arguments against Tennessee's law no longer represent the United States' position and that the new Administration would not have challenged the law; the government asks the Court to decide the question rather than dismiss.
The Court affirms the Sixth Circuit in United States v. Skrmetti by a 6-3 vote, upholding Tennessee's law.

Department of Education v. Career Colleges and Schools of Texas is dismissed under Supreme Court Rule 46 after the parties filed a joint stipulation of dismissal on 2025-08-08; merits briefing had been resumed by order of 2025-06-23.

Reuters reports that White House Counsel David Warrington will leave for the private sector and that Will Scharf will become White House Counsel effective 2026-09-01; the report does not describe the office's litigation role.

title: Have the Counsel review pending litigation and recommend reversing prior positions
uncertainties: The Skrmetti letter was read on supremecourt.gov. The abeyance motions and the Court's orders were read through SCOTUSblog case-file docket summaries, not the supremecourt.gov docket pages. Only the Education and Calumet rulings on the abeyance motions were checked; outcomes in the other two cases were not. The record covers a few Supreme Court cases from the first weeks; lower-court position changes were not surveyed. Nothing found shows what the White House Counsel recommended or when, so the match is partial and progress is held at the low end of implemented (inference): the outcome the chapter describes is visible, the Counsel's process is not. Court outcomes after the pause are context, not outcomes of the recommendation.
